question: Can changes of measurement units be formalized as an exact noncompact group action and imposed on arbitrary regressors by learning only from dimensionless invariants?

key_findings.claim: A lightweight featurizer-decoder construction makes any intervening regression model exactly units equivariant.
key_findings.evidence: Integer unit vectors define an action of positive base-unit scalings; Smith-normal-form lattice solutions produce dimensionless Laurent monomials, while a decoder multiplies the dimensionless prediction by an input monomial with the output's dimensions.

key_findings.claim: Dimensional constraints can reduce a symbolic feature space by orders of magnitude.
key_findings.evidence: For the springy double-pendulum Hamiltonian, degree-bounded construction yields 286 dimensionless monomials versus 187,500 unrestricted monomials; the restricted linear fit recovers the exact Hamiltonian at machine precision, while adding 500 random dimensional terms worsens error by about an order of magnitude.

key_findings.claim: Exact unit rescaling generalizes by construction, and the pendulum experiment confirms this under a controlled shift.
key_findings.evidence: In-distribution relative error is 0.0061 dimensionless versus 0.0055 baseline, but after multiplying every mass-dimensional input by a random factor the errors are 0.0089 versus 0.3669; a broader parameter shift yields 0.0435 versus 0.1885.

key_findings.claim: Smaller natural-science examples also show useful inductive bias.
key_findings.evidence: On the Rietkerk vegetation emulator, the dimensionless linear regression reduces test MSE from 26.3 to 12.6 and increases Pearson correlation from 0.94 to 0.97 using fewer features.

key_findings.claim: The real noncompact-scaling case lacks the clean generalization theorem invoked from compact-group equivariance.
key_findings.evidence: No scaling-invariant probability distribution exists, and Reynolds and L2-orthogonal projections do not coincide for any real measure; the paper proves a related result only after complexification and explicitly leaves rigorous OOD theory open.

key_findings.claim: Exact units consistency can be exactly wrong when the variable inventory is incomplete.
key_findings.evidence: Without Planck's dimensional constant h, the construction permits only the Rayleigh-Jeans form and cannot fit black-body radiation; the framework has no procedure to discover the missing constant.

method.core_idea: Canonicalize a physical learning problem into dimensionless invariant coordinates, run an ordinary model in that quotient space, and restore output units through a deterministic equivariant decoder.
method.mechanism: Represent each variable's dimensions as an integer exponent vector, solve integer null-space equations for invariant Laurent monomials, choose a dimensional output monomial, train on invariant features, and optionally combine with rotation/permutation invariant scalarization.
assumptions: Every relevant input and output has known, coherent units.
All dimensional constants needed by the physical law are supplied.
Integer-power Laurent monomials form a usable invariant coordinate system on the domain.
Zeros and sign changes do not make negative-power features singular.
Unit rescaling is an exact symmetry of the target and measurement process.

techniques.role: Formalizes passive base-unit changes as exact equivariance.
Computes a lattice basis of dimensionless integer-power monomials.
Restores the target's unit representation after dimensionless inference.
Combines units symmetry with coordinate-free vector inner products.
Separates exact conversion generalization from ordinary parameter extrapolation.

evaluations.setting: Hamiltonian symbolic regression for a spring and a springy double pendulum.
evaluations.metric: Feature count, held-out MSE, and coefficient recovery.
evaluations.result: Dimensionless features shrink the search dramatically and recover the correct expression at machine precision in the reported examples.
evaluations.baseline: Degree-matched unrestricted rational monomials and a mixed feature set.

evaluations.metric: Geometric mean state-relative error over 60 time points and ten trials.
evaluations.result: The dimensionless Hamiltonian MLP is similar in-distribution and far better under unit and parameter shifts.
evaluations.baseline: Parameter-matched scalar Hamiltonian MLP using dimensional features.

evaluations.metric: Test MSE and Pearson correlation for 200-day average vegetation.
evaluations.result: Units-equivariant linear regression obtains 12.6 MSE and 0.97 correlation versus 26.3 and 0.94.
evaluations.baseline: Linear regression on dimensional parameters, inverses, and intercept.

evaluations.metric: Whether allowed dimensionless features can represent the observed law.
evaluations.result: The method reproduces the long-wavelength classical form but fails on the full spectrum unless Planck's constant is supplied.

limitations: Author-stated: users must supply coherent units and a comprehensive list of dimensional constants.
Author-stated: the framework neither learns dimensions nor discovers missing constants or dimensionless inputs.
Author-stated: units equivariance is weak when inputs share one unit or relevant physical quantities are unknown.
Reviewer inference: integer Laurent features can be singular at zero and poorly conditioned over wide dynamic ranges.
Reviewer inference: choosing a finite invariant basis, degree bound, decoder monomial, and base-unit independence introduces design choices not resolved by the theorem.
Reviewer inference: most empirical gains come from small simulators and controlled shifts rather than noisy, heterogeneous observational data.
failure_modes: A missing physical constant makes every admissible model systematically misspecified.
Incorrect metadata labels a merely correlated variable as dimensionally commensurate.
Negative powers explode near zero or turn measurement noise into heavy-tailed features.
Dimensionless ratios collapse information when the target depends on an omitted scale-setting variable.
The declared base dimensions are artificially independent or dependent, changing the invariant lattice.
A unit-consistent relation remains scientifically wrong because dimensional analysis constrains form but not dynamics.
reusable_insights: Treat unit changes as a software contract: the same physical example in any coherent unit system should transform outputs exactly.
Dimensionless canonicalization can be composed with almost any downstream model and tested independently of it.
A failed units-aware fit is diagnostically useful: it can signal an omitted dimensional constant or variable.
Controlled unit conversion and genuine physical parameter extrapolation should be reported as separate OOD tests.
open_questions: Can units or missing dimensional constants be inferred jointly with the predictive model?
How can invariant coordinates avoid negative-power singularities and severe conditioning?
What finite-sample or domain-adaptation guarantee applies to real noncompact unit scalings?
Can the method handle uncertain, affine, logarithmic, or context-dependent units such as Celsius and decibels?
How much does exact units equivariance help on noisy scientific observations rather than simulator outputs?

competitive_landscape.title: Dimensionally Consistent Learning with Buckingham Pi
competitive_landscape.difference: Bakarji et al. propose constrained nonparametric fitting, BuckiNet, and dimensionless SINDy; the reviewed paper gives a general group-equivariant wrapper and integer-lattice construction applicable beyond those three learners.

competitive_landscape.title: AI Feynman: a Physics-Inspired Method for Symbolic Regression
competitive_landscape.difference: AI Feynman combines several physics-inspired decompositions to recover equations; the reviewed approach isolates exact unit symmetry and can wrap arbitrary regressors rather than supplying a full symbolic search algorithm.

competitive_landscape.title: Deep symbolic regression for physics guided by units constraints: toward the automated discovery of physical laws
competitive_landscape.difference: Phi-SO embeds dimensional grammar directly in reinforcement-learning expression generation and handles substantial noise; the reviewed method learns in precomputed invariant coordinates and cannot discover missing constants.

competitive_landscape.title: Enhancing Symbolic Regression and Universal Physics-Informed Neural Networks with Dimensional Analysis
competitive_landscape.difference: Podina et al. integrate Buckingham/Ipsen normalization with AI Feynman and UPINNs for hidden differential terms, extending dimensional reduction to equation discovery beyond the reviewed toy regressions.

competitive_landscape.title: Dimensionless Policies based on the Buckingham pi Theorem: Is This a Good Way to Generalize Numerical Results?
competitive_landscape.difference: Gonzalez and colleagues apply dimensionless policies to numerical control and exact transfer across similar systems; the reviewed paper focuses on regression, emulation, and symbolic relations.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: Units covariance is an exact noncompact symmetry that can be imposed broadly through algorithmically constructed invariants and an output decoder, improving sample efficiency and OOD behavior.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper supplies the group formulation, integer-lattice implementation, extensive mathematical appendix, controlled emulator tests, and a deliberately failing missing-constant example.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The general equivariant wrapper and careful failure analysis are strong contributions, though Buckingham-Pi learning is concurrent prior art. The empirical case is convincing for exact unit conversion but preliminary for broad scientific OOD generalization.

reviewer_notes: Read all 32 extracted pages, including the noncompact-group appendix, numerical tables, and black-body counterexample. Competing dimensional-learning and units-aware symbolic-regression papers were checked at primary arXiv records on 2026-08-23.
